// Characterization test for the shortlist.js empty-state fix: a shortlist
// API response with no data can mean "no scan has ever run" (data.generated
// is null) OR "a scan completed and legitimately found zero candidates"
// (data.result === 'no_candidates', data.generated is a real timestamp).
// Before this fix both cases showed the identical "no scan has run" banner,
// making a normal zero-candidate trading day look indistinguishable from a
// broken pipeline — and the empty state never surfaced pageMeta's generated
// timestamp at all. See .sprint/SPRINT_PLAN.md (TASK-003) for the bug report.
//
// Mocks shortlist.js's imports (fetchJSON, DOM, core/ui-helpers) and calls
// the real renderShortlistView(), matching this repo's no-framework/no-build
// testing style — same "extract/mock and eval" approach as the other files
// in this directory, just at module granularity since this function needs
// its real module-level imports resolved, not just its own function body.
//
// Run with: node tests/js/test_shortlist_empty_state.js

const assert = require('assert');
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');
const os = require('os');

function fakeEl() {
  return { innerHTML: '', textContent: '', style: {}, addEventListener: () => {}, querySelectorAll: () => [] };
}

async function renderScenario(scenario, responses) {
  const elements = {};
  global.document = { getElementById: (id) => (elements[id] ||= fakeEl()), querySelectorAll: () => [] };
  global.window = {};
  global.location = { href: 'http://localhost/' };
  global.fetch = async () => ({ json: async () => ({}) });

  const contentEl = fakeEl();
  const pageMetaEl = fakeEl();

  global.__mockFetchJSON = async (url) => {
    if (url === '/api/shortlist') return responses[scenario];
    if (url === '/api/top20') return { generated: responses[scenario].generated, top20: [{ ticker: 'AAPL', score: 80 }] };
    return {};
  };
  global.__mockContent = contentEl;
  global.__mockPageMeta = pageMetaEl;
  global.__mockCurrentView = 'shortlist';

  const srcPath = path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'static', 'js', 'views', 'shortlist.js');
  const src = fs.readFileSync(srcPath, 'utf8');

  const patched = src
    .replace("import { fetchJSON } from '../core/api.js';", 'const fetchJSON = global.__mockFetchJSON;')
    .replace("import { startJob } from '../core/jobs.js';", 'const startJob = async () => {};')
    .replace("import { _liveGuarded, _startLive } from '../core/refresh.js';", 'const _liveGuarded = async () => {}; const _startLive = () => {};')
    .replace("import { content, currentView, pageMeta } from '../core/state.js';", 'const content = global.__mockContent; const currentView = global.__mockCurrentView; const pageMeta = global.__mockPageMeta;')
    .replace(/import \{[\s\S]*?\} from '..\/core\/ui-helpers.js';/, `
      const chartToggleButtonHTML = () => '';
      const escapeHtml = (s) => s;
      const fidelityLink = () => '';
      const loadMomentumStatus = () => {};
      const paintMomentumSlots = () => {};
      const refreshOpenCharts = () => {};
      const renderTop20Table = (top20) => '<table data-top20-count="' + top20.length + '"></table>';
      const wireChartToggles = () => {};
    `);

  const tmpFile = path.join(os.tmpdir(), `shortlist_patched_${scenario}.mjs`);
  fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, patched);
  const mod = await import(`file://${tmpFile}`);
  await mod.renderShortlistView();
  fs.unlinkSync(tmpFile);

  return { pageMetaText: pageMetaEl.textContent, bannerHTML: contentEl.innerHTML };
}

async function main() {
  const responses = {
    'never-scanned': { generated: null, result: null, shortlist: [], fundamentals_audits: {}, catalyst_sentiments: {}, congress_signals: {} },
    'zero-candidates': { generated: '2026-09-14T12:00:00', result: 'no_candidates', shortlist: [], fundamentals_audits: {}, catalyst_sentiments: {}, congress_signals: {} },
  };

  const neverScanned = await renderScenario('never-scanned', responses);
  assert.strictEqual(neverScanned.pageMetaText, '', 'no-scan-ever case should show no generated timestamp');
  assert.ok(neverScanned.bannerHTML.includes('No filtered shortlist yet'),
    'no-scan-ever case should show the generic "run a scan" banner');

  const zeroCandidates = await renderScenario('zero-candidates', responses);
  assert.ok(zeroCandidates.pageMetaText.includes('Generated'),
    'zero-candidates case must surface the real generated timestamp (this was the bug: pageMeta was only set in the non-empty branch)');
  assert.ok(zeroCandidates.bannerHTML.includes('found no candidates'),
    'zero-candidates case must show a distinct message, not the generic "no scan has run" banner');
  assert.ok(!zeroCandidates.bannerHTML.includes('No filtered shortlist yet'),
    'zero-candidates case must NOT show the "run a scan" banner — a scan DID run');

  console.log('test_shortlist_empty_state.js: all assertions passed');
}

main().catch(e => { console.error('FAILED:', e.message); process.exit(1); });

// Characterization test for startJob — moved to static/js/core/jobs.js by
// TASK-003 (router/jobs/refresh extraction). Locks in the fix from earlier
// this session where startJob's returned promise now resolves only on job
// completion, not right after the initial POST. Every _liveGuarded caller
// depends on this to know when it's actually safe to start the next refresh
// cycle; regressing this silently defeats that guard again (it happened once
// already — see the git history for "_liveGuarded doesn't actually await job
// completion").
//
// Plain Node, no test framework/dependency. Run with: node tests/js/test_start_job.js

const assert = require('assert');
const fs = require('fs');
const path = require('path');

const src = fs.readFileSync(
  path.join(__dirname, '..', '..', 'static', 'js', 'core', 'jobs.js'), 'utf8'
);

function extract(fnName) {
  let start = src.indexOf(`function ${fnName}(`);
  if (start === -1) throw new Error(`${fnName} not found in dashboard.js`);
  if (src.slice(Math.max(0, start - 6), start) === 'async ') start -= 6;
  let depth = 0, i = src.indexOf('{', start);
  for (; i < src.length; i++) {
    if (src[i] === '{') depth++;
    if (src[i] === '}') { depth--; if (depth === 0) break; }
  }
  return src.slice(start, i + 1);
}

async function main() {
  // Mock fetchJSON: first call is the POST (returns job_id), subsequent
  // calls are polls returning a scripted status sequence.
  const statusSequence = ['queued', 'running', 'running', 'success'];
  let pollCount = 0;
  let postCalled = false;

  global.fetchJSON = async (url, opts) => {
    if (opts && opts.method === 'POST') {
      postCalled = true;
      return { job_id: 'test-job-1' };
    }
    const status = statusSequence[Math.min(pollCount, statusSequence.length - 1)];
    pollCount++;
    return { status, output: [] };
  };

  // startJob's internal setTimeout(poll, 1500) would make this test slow —
  // replace with immediate scheduling for the test only.
  global.setTimeout = (fn) => fn();

  eval(extract('startJob'));

  const updates = [];
  let resolvedBeforeTerminal = false;

  const jobPromise = startJob('test-kind', {}, (st) => {
    updates.push(st.status);
    if (st.status === 'running' || st.status === 'queued') {
      // If the promise has already resolved while we're still seeing
      // non-terminal statuses, the fix regressed.
    }
  });

  const resolvedJobId = await jobPromise;

  assert.strictEqual(postCalled, true, 'startJob must POST to start the job');
  assert.strictEqual(resolvedJobId, 'test-job-1', 'startJob must resolve with the job_id');
  assert.deepStrictEqual(
    updates, ['queued', 'running', 'running', 'success'],
    'onUpdate must have been called once per poll, ending with the terminal status'
  );
  // The critical regression check: the promise must not have resolved until
  // the LAST onUpdate call (the terminal one) had already fired.
  assert.strictEqual(
    updates[updates.length - 1], 'success',
    'the last onUpdate call before resolution must be the terminal status — ' +
    'if this fails, startJob is resolving early again (the exact bug fixed this session)'
  );

  console.log('test_start_job.js: all assertions passed');
}

main().catch(e => { console.error('FAILED:', e.message); process.exit(1); });

Both `current_price` (already computed as a local variable during scanning) and the equivalent for shortlist items are **not currently persisted** to `top20_latest.json`/`shortlist_latest.json` — adding it is a small, additive backend change, not a new fetch. This satisfies the user's 3rd request for both views with a single change.
 
 ## Tasks
 
-- TASK-001 | Claude | **Urgent**: fix the workflow timeout regression (raise `timeout-minutes`, add safety margin above observed runtime) | no deps
-- TASK-002 | Codex | Atomic JSON writes + explicit result state (`success`/`no_candidates`) in `run_optimized_scan.py`'s output, so "legitimately empty" is distinguishable from "broken" | no deps
-- TASK-003 | Claude | Fix `shortlist.js` empty-state: show `generated` timestamp always, distinguish "no data yet" vs "zero candidates today" | deps: 002 (consumes the result-state field)
-- TASK-004 | Claude | Surface data freshness (shortlist's own `generated` date) near the Sync button, so this exact confusion — "sync says up to date" vs "data looks old" — is legible to the user going forward | deps: 003
-- TASK-005 | Claude | Verification: after TASK-001 lands on `main`, manually trigger the workflow (`gh workflow run` / `workflow_dispatch`) and confirm end-to-end — completes within the new timeout, writes fresh data, commits, pushes, dashboard picks it up — without waiting for tomorrow's cron | deps: 001, 002, 003, 004
+- TASK-001 | Codex | Persist `current_price` on buy/sell signals (`run_optimized_scan.py`) and shortlist items — small backend addition, no behavior change otherwise | no deps
+- TASK-002 | Claude | `charts.js`: new `renderMarketScatterChart` (global function, design-token colors, RS=0 reference line, tooltip) + supporting CSS (chart wrapper sizing, must have explicit height per Chart.js's `maintainAspectRatio:false` collapse gotcha both agents flagged) | no deps
+- TASK-003 | Claude | `market.js`: wire the scatter chart into its new placement, hover tooltip, click→jump+highlight+tab-switch, display `current_price` on rows/Top 20 | deps: 002
+- TASK-004 | Codex | `market.js`: replace the two stacked Buy/Sell tables with the ARIA-tablist toggle registry | deps: 003 (same file — sequential, not parallel, per the lesson from the last sprint about concurrent edits to one file)
+- TASK-005 | Claude | `shortlist.js`: display `current_price` on pick cards | deps: 001 (different file — can run in parallel with 002/003/004)
+- TASK-006 | Claude | Tests (JS characterization tests for the pure point-building/tab-state helpers, matching this repo's extract-and-eval/mock-and-import style) + final verification (module-graph load check, HTTP checks, accessibility spot-check of the new tablist pattern) | deps: 003, 004, 005
 
 ## Explicitly out of scope for this sprint
 
-- Reducing the scan's actual ~63-minute runtime (Codex flagged this as worth
-  profiling long-term; not blocking, not part of this fix).
-- Rebuilding the sync mechanism around commit SHAs instead of `git pull`
-  output-string parsing (Codex's suggestion — a good idea, bigger than this
-  bug fix warrants right now).
-- A full run-status manifest / observability system (Codex's fuller proposal;
-  TASK-002 covers the minimal version actually needed to fix the reported bug).
-- Migrating off git-based storage to a database/object store (architecturally
-  cleaner per Codex, but far more than this fix needs).
+- Persisting the full (400+) signal universe instead of the current top 50/30 cap — a separate, real backend change (structured JSON output from the scanner) that both Codex and this plan flag as a legitimate future enhancement, not silently included here.
+- Any change to the actual scan/scoring logic, `rs`/`score` computation, or `entry_quality` classification.
+- A general accessible alternative-representation system beyond what the existing table already provides (the table remains the screen-reader-equivalent detail view; the chart is a visual shortcut, not a replacement).

    60	def _fetch_headlines(ticker: str, limit: int = MAX_HEADLINES) -> List[Dict]:
    61	    """Recent news headlines via yfinance. Never raises."""
    62	    try:
    63	        news = yf.Ticker(ticker).news or []
    64	    except Exception as e:
    65	        logger.debug(f"News fetch failed for {ticker}: {e}")
    66	        return []
    67	
    68	    headlines = []
    69	    for item in news[:limit]:
    70	        content = item.get("content", {})
    71	        title = content.get("title")
    72	        publisher = (content.get("provider") or {}).get("displayName")
    73	        pub_date = content.get("pubDate")
    74	        url = (content.get("canonicalUrl") or {}).get("url")
    75	        if title:
    76	            headlines.append({"title": title, "publisher": publisher, "pub_date": pub_date, "url": url})
    77	    return headlines

     1	// --- "Live" auto-refresh -------------------------------------------------
     2	// This is a local, single-user Flask app with no push/streaming layer, so
     3	// "live" here means: while a view that supports it is open, quietly re-pull
     4	// fresh data on a timer and patch it into the DOM. Stopped on every route
     5	// change so a background view never keeps polling once you've navigated away.
     6	
     7	export const LIVE_INTERVAL_MS = 90 * 1000; // 90 seconds — cheap yfinance-only pulls, no LLM cost
     8	let _liveTimer = null;
     9	
    10	export function _stopLive() {
    11	  if (_liveTimer) { clearInterval(_liveTimer); _liveTimer = null; }
    12	}
    13	export function _startLive(fn) {
    14	  _stopLive();
    15	  _liveTimer = setInterval(fn, LIVE_INTERVAL_MS);
    16	}
    17	export function liveBadgeHTML() {
    18	  return '<span class="live-badge"><span class="live-dot"></span>Live — updates every 90s</span>';
    19	}
    20	
    21	// If a live-refresh tick's job hasn't finished by the time the next tick
    22	// fires (e.g. yfinance is slow), skip that tick instead of stacking another
    23	// overlapping job on top — the next one will pick up fresh data anyway.
    24	const _liveInFlight = new Set();
    25	export async function _liveGuarded(key, fn) {
    26	  if (_liveInFlight.has(key)) return;
    27	  _liveInFlight.add(key);
    28	  try {
    29	    await fn();
    30	  } finally {
    31	    _liveInFlight.delete(key);
    32	  }
    33	}

## Recommendation

Use a shared, progressively disclosed news component:

- Show the newest **2 headlines per ticker** by default.
- Keep all shortlist tickers visible.
- Provide a per-ticker **“Show 3 more” / “Show fewer”** button.
- Sort headlines newest-first using `pub_date`.
- On Market, additionally limit the initial ticker cards to **8 per news group**, with “Show N more tickers” for unusually large position lists.
- Preserve expanded state through the 90-second refresh.
- Add a “Jump to news” button near the top of Shortlist because expanded price charts can push the section far down.

## 1. Actual problem

This is more than simply “too many headlines.”

The current renderer in [market.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/market.js:101) has three related problems:

- Volume: every returned headline is displayed immediately.
- Weak hierarchy: ticker, title, publisher, and date are present, but all headlines have almost identical visual weight.
- Unclear ordering: dates are displayed, but the UI neither sorts explicitly nor says “newest first.”
- Poor access: Shortlist news sits after all pick cards and any expanded price charts in [shortlist.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/shortlist.js:123).

One important correction to the premise: the dashboard currently fetches **5 headlines per ticker**, not 10–20. [fetch_news.py](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/scripts/fetch_news.py:30) explicitly calls `_fetch_headlines(..., limit=5)`. The saved news batches confirm five items for almost every ticker.

That still means:

- Shortlist: normally 25 headlines.
- Market buy news: up to 40 headlines because Market selects eight Top 20 tickers at [market.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/market.js:66).
- Market positions: five headlines multiplied by an effectively unbounded number of positions.

The available headline shape is exactly:

```js
{
  title,
  publisher,
  pub_date,
  url
}
```

There is no per-headline sentiment, relevance, importance score, summary, or category. Therefore the UI can honestly identify the **newest** article, but it cannot identify the “most important” one without a backend/data-model change. The catalyst score elsewhere is ticker-level analysis, not a score for each headline.

## 2. Concrete redesign

Each ticker should become a visually bounded card:

- Header: ticker, total headline count, and optionally the newest article’s date.
- Body: newest two headlines.
- Footer: `Show 3 more` when additional items exist.
- Expanded state: all available headlines, with `Show fewer`.
- Headline rows: clearer spacing, source/date metadata, hover treatment, and a subtle “Latest” label on the first valid dated item.
- Titles: visually clamp to three lines while retaining the complete text in the DOM for assistive technology.
- Section subtitle: “Newest headlines first · 2 shown per ticker.”

Sort a copied array by parsed `pub_date`, descending. Valid dates come first; missing or invalid dates remain afterward in their original relative order. Do not mutate the API response.

I would not introduce pagination or a modal. Five items per ticker is too little to justify either, and both make cross-ticker scanning slower.

## 3. Shortlist versus Market

The same component should serve both views, but accept presentation limits.

Shortlist configuration:

- Show all five ticker cards.
- Show two headlines per ticker.
- Preserve shortlist ranking/order rather than alphabetizing tickers.
- Add a top-of-page “Jump to news” button.

Market configuration:

- Show two headlines per ticker.
- Initially show eight ticker cards per news group.
- Add a section-level “Show N more tickers” only when the group exceeds eight.
- The buy group currently contains at most eight tickers, so this second control mainly protects large position portfolios.

This gives the views a consistent interaction model while acknowledging their different scale. I would not create two unrelated renderers.

The Shortlist shortcut should be a real button calling `scrollIntoView()`, not an `href="#shortlistNews"` link: this application already uses the URL hash for routing (`#/shortlist`), so a second hash-style anchor risks interfering with navigation.

## 4. Files/modules to touch

After the active Market sprint finishes:

- [static/js/views/market.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/market.js:54)
- [static/js/views/shortlist.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/shortlist.js:16)
- [static/js/dashboard.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/dashboard.js:13)
- [static/css/dashboard.css](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/css/dashboard.css:239)
- New `static/js/components/news.js`
- New `tests/js/test_news_component.js`

The cleanest long-term structure is to move `_newsSectionHTML`, `_loadNewsGroup`, rendering, event wiring, and news UI state into `components/news.js`. Market and Shortlist can then import the shared component directly. That also removes `configureShortlistNews`, whose dependency injection currently exists only because the shared implementation lives in the Market view.

No backend change is needed for this redesign.

## 5. Implementation approach

A CSS-only `max-height` plus fade is insufficient. Headline titles have variable height, CSS cannot accurately say “Show 3 more,” and a silent refresh would still replace the DOM.

Use small, explicit JS state:

```js
Map<group, {
  expandedTickers: Set<ticker>,
  showAllTickers: boolean
}>
```

Recommended flow:

1. `_loadNewsGroup` receives rendering options such as `headlineLimit: 2` and `tickerLimit`.
2. Normalize and sort the data.
3. Render from the current group state.
4. Use one delegated click listener on the persistent `news-${group}-body` element.
5. Toggling updates the state and rerenders that group.
6. A non-silent initial load resets that group to collapsed defaults.
7. A silent refresh retains state and prunes tickers that no longer exist.

The existing 90-second path always executes:

```js
el.innerHTML = _renderNewsGroupHTML(...)
```

at [market.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/market.js:92). A naive toggle based only on DOM styles would therefore collapse everything on every refresh.

Two additional refinements are worthwhile:

- Cache normalized data and skip `innerHTML` replacement if the refresh returned identical content.
- If replacement is required while a toggle owns focus, restore focus to the corresponding new toggle afterward.

The existing `toggleReasons` pattern demonstrates the desired compact control, but it should not be reused unchanged. Its state exists only in inline styles, its collapsed label is not restored correctly after reopening/closing cycles, and it has no `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls`.

News controls should use:

```html
<button
  type="button"
  aria-expanded="false"
  aria-controls="news-shortlist-NGL-extra">
  Show 3 more
</button>
```

The controlled content should use the native `hidden` attribute.

## 6. Alternatives rejected

- **CSS max-height/fade:** clips unpredictably because titles vary in length and cannot survive DOM replacement as meaningful state.
- **Modal:** hides ticker context and makes comparing five shortlist candidates cumbersome.
- **Pagination:** excessive for five items per ticker and creates unnecessary navigation.
- **One global chronological feed:** makes recency clearer but loses the per-pick organization the user needs when evaluating a shortlist.
- **Only one open ticker accordion:** reduces height aggressively but adds repetitive clicks during daily comparison.
- **“Important news” ranking:** unsupported by the current data. Recency is the only defensible ordering signal.
- **Backend fetch reduction from five to two:** saves little and prevents instant expansion. Fetch five, initially display two.
- **Moving news above the picks:** would make news easier to reach but demote the primary shortlist decision cards. A jump control solves access without changing information priority.

## 7. Risks

- Silent refresh can lose expanded state unless it is stored outside the DOM.
- DOM replacement can also lose keyboard focus or shift the page.
- Invalid `pub_date` values can produce `Invalid Date` unless parsed defensively.
- Missing URLs currently deserve special attention: `safeHref(undefined)` can resolve as a relative URL rather than representing “no link.” A headline without a valid HTTP(S) URL should render as non-clickable text.
- Long titles can produce uneven card heights; line clamping should be visual only.
- Two layers of disclosure on Market—more headlines and more tickers—must use explicit labels so they are not confused.
- Module-level state can survive route changes longer than desired. Reset on the next non-silent view load, but preserve it during silent refreshes.
- Expanded content changing during refresh can cause scroll movement.

## 8. Edge cases

- **No tickers supplied:** retain the existing contextual empty message.
- **Empty news object:** retain “No news found.”
- **Ticker with zero headlines:** retain a visible ticker card saying “No recent headlines”; do not silently hide it.
- **Exactly one or two headlines:** show them with no expansion button.
- **Missing/invalid date:** place after valid dated articles and omit the date label.
- **Equal dates:** preserve feed order with a stable sort.
- **Ticker missing from the response:** render it from the requested ticker order with an empty state. The current renderer uses only `Object.keys(newsByTicker)`, so a missing response key disappears entirely.
- **Duplicate headlines within one ticker:** deduplicate by canonical URL, falling back to normalized title.
- **Duplicate headline across different tickers:** keep it in each ticker card; removing it globally could conceal why it is relevant to another holding.
- **Missing publisher:** retain “Unknown source.”
- **Missing title:** drop the malformed item defensively.
- **Unsafe or absent URL:** non-clickable headline rather than a misleading `#` link.

## Recommendation

Use a shared, progressively disclosed news component:

- Show the newest **2 headlines per ticker** by default.
- Keep all shortlist tickers visible.
- Provide a per-ticker **“Show 3 more” / “Show fewer”** button.
- Sort headlines newest-first using `pub_date`.
- On Market, additionally limit the initial ticker cards to **8 per news group**, with “Show N more tickers” for unusually large position lists.
- Preserve expanded state through the 90-second refresh.
- Add a “Jump to news” button near the top of Shortlist because expanded price charts can push the section far down.

## 1. Actual problem

This is more than simply “too many headlines.”

The current renderer in [market.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/market.js:101) has three related problems:

- Volume: every returned headline is displayed immediately.
- Weak hierarchy: ticker, title, publisher, and date are present, but all headlines have almost identical visual weight.
- Unclear ordering: dates are displayed, but the UI neither sorts explicitly nor says “newest first.”
- Poor access: Shortlist news sits after all pick cards and any expanded price charts in [shortlist.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/shortlist.js:123).

One important correction to the premise: the dashboard currently fetches **5 headlines per ticker**, not 10–20. [fetch_news.py](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/scripts/fetch_news.py:30) explicitly calls `_fetch_headlines(..., limit=5)`. The saved news batches confirm five items for almost every ticker.

That still means:

- Shortlist: normally 25 headlines.
- Market buy news: up to 40 headlines because Market selects eight Top 20 tickers at [market.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/market.js:66).
- Market positions: five headlines multiplied by an effectively unbounded number of positions.

The available headline shape is exactly:

```js
{
  title,
  publisher,
  pub_date,
  url
}
```

There is no per-headline sentiment, relevance, importance score, summary, or category. Therefore the UI can honestly identify the **newest** article, but it cannot identify the “most important” one without a backend/data-model change. The catalyst score elsewhere is ticker-level analysis, not a score for each headline.

## 2. Concrete redesign

Each ticker should become a visually bounded card:

- Header: ticker, total headline count, and optionally the newest article’s date.
- Body: newest two headlines.
- Footer: `Show 3 more` when additional items exist.
- Expanded state: all available headlines, with `Show fewer`.
- Headline rows: clearer spacing, source/date metadata, hover treatment, and a subtle “Latest” label on the first valid dated item.
- Titles: visually clamp to three lines while retaining the complete text in the DOM for assistive technology.
- Section subtitle: “Newest headlines first · 2 shown per ticker.”

Sort a copied array by parsed `pub_date`, descending. Valid dates come first; missing or invalid dates remain afterward in their original relative order. Do not mutate the API response.

I would not introduce pagination or a modal. Five items per ticker is too little to justify either, and both make cross-ticker scanning slower.

## 3. Shortlist versus Market

The same component should serve both views, but accept presentation limits.

Shortlist configuration:

- Show all five ticker cards.
- Show two headlines per ticker.
- Preserve shortlist ranking/order rather than alphabetizing tickers.
- Add a top-of-page “Jump to news” button.

Market configuration:

- Show two headlines per ticker.
- Initially show eight ticker cards per news group.
- Add a section-level “Show N more tickers” only when the group exceeds eight.
- The buy group currently contains at most eight tickers, so this second control mainly protects large position portfolios.

This gives the views a consistent interaction model while acknowledging their different scale. I would not create two unrelated renderers.

The Shortlist shortcut should be a real button calling `scrollIntoView()`, not an `href="#shortlistNews"` link: this application already uses the URL hash for routing (`#/shortlist`), so a second hash-style anchor risks interfering with navigation.

## 4. Files/modules to touch

After the active Market sprint finishes:

- [static/js/views/market.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/market.js:54)
- [static/js/views/shortlist.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/shortlist.js:16)
- [static/js/dashboard.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/dashboard.js:13)
- [static/css/dashboard.css](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/css/dashboard.css:239)
- New `static/js/components/news.js`
- New `tests/js/test_news_component.js`

The cleanest long-term structure is to move `_newsSectionHTML`, `_loadNewsGroup`, rendering, event wiring, and news UI state into `components/news.js`. Market and Shortlist can then import the shared component directly. That also removes `configureShortlistNews`, whose dependency injection currently exists only because the shared implementation lives in the Market view.

No backend change is needed for this redesign.

## 5. Implementation approach

A CSS-only `max-height` plus fade is insufficient. Headline titles have variable height, CSS cannot accurately say “Show 3 more,” and a silent refresh would still replace the DOM.

Use small, explicit JS state:

```js
Map<group, {
  expandedTickers: Set<ticker>,
  showAllTickers: boolean
}>
```

Recommended flow:

1. `_loadNewsGroup` receives rendering options such as `headlineLimit: 2` and `tickerLimit`.
2. Normalize and sort the data.
3. Render from the current group state.
4. Use one delegated click listener on the persistent `news-${group}-body` element.
5. Toggling updates the state and rerenders that group.
6. A non-silent initial load resets that group to collapsed defaults.
7. A silent refresh retains state and prunes tickers that no longer exist.

The existing 90-second path always executes:

```js
el.innerHTML = _renderNewsGroupHTML(...)
```

at [market.js](/Users/badripratti/Desktop/stock-screener/static/js/views/market.js:92). A naive toggle based only on DOM styles would therefore collapse everything on every refresh.

Two additional refinements are worthwhile:

- Cache normalized data and skip `innerHTML` replacement if the refresh returned identical content.
- If replacement is required while a toggle owns focus, restore focus to the corresponding new toggle afterward.

The existing `toggleReasons` pattern demonstrates the desired compact control, but it should not be reused unchanged. Its state exists only in inline styles, its collapsed label is not restored correctly after reopening/closing cycles, and it has no `aria-expanded` or `aria-controls`.

News controls should use:

```html
<button
  type="button"
  aria-expanded="false"
  aria-controls="news-shortlist-NGL-extra">
  Show 3 more
</button>
```

The controlled content should use the native `hidden` attribute.

## 6. Alternatives rejected

- **CSS max-height/fade:** clips unpredictably because titles vary in length and cannot survive DOM replacement as meaningful state.
- **Modal:** hides ticker context and makes comparing five shortlist candidates cumbersome.
- **Pagination:** excessive for five items per ticker and creates unnecessary navigation.
- **One global chronological feed:** makes recency clearer but loses the per-pick organization the user needs when evaluating a shortlist.
- **Only one open ticker accordion:** reduces height aggressively but adds repetitive clicks during daily comparison.
- **“Important news” ranking:** unsupported by the current data. Recency is the only defensible ordering signal.
- **Backend fetch reduction from five to two:** saves little and prevents instant expansion. Fetch five, initially display two.
- **Moving news above the picks:** would make news easier to reach but demote the primary shortlist decision cards. A jump control solves access without changing information priority.
